results.fact: Rope set-up for the Eye Col gully descent
results.evidence: The reported East Twin Needle descent (downclimb and rappel to Eye Col, then several rappels down the south gullies to Crescent Creek Basin) gives no rope length or single-vs-double setup. The only published double-60 m account is for the Himmelhorn-West Twin Needle notch exit, not the Eye Col gullies. No source states the gullies go on a single rope, so gear[1]/rack[4]/rappels/detailed_rack (two ropes) vs descent_text/rope_note (single rope for the gullies) cannot be settled; a trip report naming the rope used on the Eye Col gully raps would settle it.

results.correct_value: waypoints[3] is the ~6,400 ft saddle camp northeast of the Chopping Block; the Crescent Creek Basin camp lies ~200+ ft lower (about 6,050 ft)
results.evidence: Two independent trip reports describe a 6,400 ft saddle northeast of the Chopping Block used as a camp, with a ~200 ft drop from it into Crescent Creek Basin; one also records a basin camp below Mount Terror at 6,050 ft. So the 6,400 ft waypoint is the saddle camp and its basin label is the error; renaming it to the saddle camp (keeping 6,400) makes it agree with the approach text, which keeps the two camps separate.

results.fact: Whether the overnight permit can be reserved in advance
results.correct_value: Terror Basin and Crescent Creek cross-country zones are walk-up only, issued in person at Marblemount the day of or the day before
results.evidence: The park's cross-country zone list says only Boston Basin, Eldorado, Sulphide, Price, Triumph and Tapto Lakes can be reserved in advance and all other zones (Terror Basin and Crescent Creek among them) are walk-up only; the park's reservations FAQ repeats this and says walk-up zones must be obtained in person the day of or day before. A Pickets trip report describes having to pick the permit up in person at the station. The route's permit and access text that offered advance reservation is patched; the sibling Frenzel Spitz row already says walk-up only.

results.fact: Which way the step below the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col is rappelled
results.correct_value: Rappelled on the way in (descending the north side toward Frenzel Spitz), reclimbed on the way back
results.evidence: A first-hand account of an attempt on Frenzel Spitz's south face describes building an equalized pin/sling/nut anchor and rappelling off the north side of the Himmelhorn/Ottohorn col into the broken couloir and glacier while heading toward the peak. A separate AAC account records a single-rope rappel from a station about 150 ft below the Otto-Himmel col when descending its north side toward the Mustard Glacier. Both place the rappel on the descent from the col, matching waypoints[6], the itinerary and descent_text.

patches.replace: the step below the col is commonly rappelled from natural anchors on the way in and reclimbed on the way back.

results.fact: Time from trailhead to Terror Basin
results.evidence: One party reached the Terror Creek crossing (~2,000 ft) only 3.9 hours from the car and the ridge crest above 6.4 hours from the car; another took 6.5 hours from the trailhead to the camp near the Chopping Block. Terror Basin (~5,700 ft) sits well above the creek, so '3+ hours' is far too short; the 7 hours in the itinerary and timing agree with the reports.

results.correct_value: About 1.5 days in and usually one long day out
results.evidence: One party walked from a Stump Hollow camp (~6,000 ft) to the car in 7.6 hours; another went from the camp near the Chopping Block to the trailhead in 4 hours; a third exited from the Crescent Creek Basin camp to the car in a single day. The itinerary (Days 1-2 in, one 9.5-hour exit day, optionally split) agrees; the 'roughly 1.5-2 days each way' in partner_requirements overstates the exit.
